# Incident Report — MTA 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** (confirmed via ARP: `10.11.26.183 -> d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b`, and matches `eth.src` on all frames sourced from this IP) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` records and mDNS/LLMNR responses from the host) |
| AD domain / workgroup | **NEMOTODES** (NetBIOS) / **nemotoads.health** (Kerberos realm `NEMOTODES.HEALTH`, LDAP SRV queries for `NEMOTODES-DC.nemotoads.health`) |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** (from `kerberos.CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic sourced from 10.11.26.183) |

## Malware family
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The traffic matches ETPRO signatures by name and content:
- `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`
- `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` / `NetSupport Remote Admin Response`
- `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`

This is corroborated directly in the packet capture: every C2 POST carries the literal HTTP User-Agent string `NetSupport Manager/1.3`, and the client performs a geolocation lookup against the vendor's own infrastructure (`geo.netsupportsoftware.com`) immediately before C2 begins — both are intrinsic, hard-coded behaviors of the genuine NetSupport client software, not spoofed indicators.

## Infection chain (grounded in traffic timestamps, UTC+4 as captured)
1. **08:50:11** — TLS session to `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5), a redirect/gate site.
2. **08:50:14** — TLS session to `confirmsubscription.com` (52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207), consistent with a browser push-notification consent scam used as a lure/redirect step.
3. **08:50:14 – 08:50:40** — Repeated TLS sessions (SNI `modandcrackedapk.com`, 193.42.38.139) — flagged by Suricata as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `... in TLS SNI`. This is a fake "cracked APK/mod" download site, the probable delivery vector for the NetSupport client installer. (Content is TLS-encrypted; no plaintext payload was recoverable from this capture.)
4. **08:50:45** — Immediately following the last `modandcrackedapk.com` connection, the host queries `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → `GET /location/loca.asp` (104.26.1.231:80), a self-check performed by the NetSupport client on startup.
5. **08:50:45 – 09:43:29** — Persistent C2 beacon: `POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` with `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, repeating roughly every 60 seconds for ~53 minutes (58 POSTs observed), all over TCP/443 in plaintext HTTP (not TLS) — matching `ET POLICY HTTP POST on unusual Port Possibly Hostile` / `ET POLICY HTTP traffic on port 443 (POST)`.

Separately and earlier in the same capture, unrelated internal SMB/NetBIOS scanning noise from 10.11.26.183 toward the domain controller (10.11.26.3) triggered `Potentially unsafe SMBv1 protocol in use` and `GPL NETBIOS SMB ... NTMLSSP ... overflow attempt` alerts around 08:50:10 UTC+4; these look like legacy SMBv1/IPC$ enumeration traffic rather than confirmed exploitation, and are noted for completeness but are **not** treated as part of the NetSupport RAT chain.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | `194.180.191.64:443` | 58+ HTTP POSTs to `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm`, UA `NetSupport Manager/1.3`, matched by ETPRO NetSupport RAT CnC signatures |

**Malicious/suspicious domains**
| Domain | Resolved IP(s) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| modandcrackedapk.com | 193.42.38.139 | DNS query + TLS SNI, flagged `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain` in both DNS and TLS SNI rules |
| classicgrand.com | 213.246.109.5 | DNS query + TLS SNI, first host contacted in the redirect chain at 08:50:11 |
| confirmsubscription.com | 13.56.30.207, 52.8.34.0 | DNS query + TLS SNI, second host in the redirect chain |
| geo.netsupportsoftware.com | 104.26.1.231, 104.26.0.231, 172.67.68.212 | Plaintext `GET /location/loca.asp`, NetSupport client's own geolocation check-in service |

**Malicious URL**
| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| URL | `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` | Repeating C2 POST target, plaintext HTTP capture, UA `NetSupport Manager/1.3` |

**Files / hashes**
No malware executable or dropper was recoverable from this capture. All plaintext HTTP object transfers observed are either benign (Microsoft connectivity/CRL checks, Adobe update check) or trivial C2 beacon responses (`fakeurl.htm`, tiny bodies, no executable content). The actual NetSupport installer/dropper was almost certainly delivered over the encrypted TLS session to `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139), which cannot be inspected without TLS key material — no file name or SHA256 hash can be truthfully asserted for the initial payload from this evidence.

**Benign context** (do not treat as IOCs): `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `r10.o.lencr.org`, `acroipm2.adobe.com`, MSN/Bing/Office/Google/jsdelivr-style CDN domains, and internal AD/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB traffic to `10.11.26.3` (domain controller `NEMOTODES-DC.nemotoads.health`).

## Summary
Windows workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as user **oboomwald** on the **NEMOTODES/nemotoads.health** domain, was infected with **NetSupport RAT** after browsing through a redirect chain (`classicgrand.com` → `confirmsubscription.com` → `modandcrackedapk.com`, a fake cracked-software/APK download site) beginning at 08:50:11 UTC+4 on 2024-11-26. Within seconds of the final visit to `modandcrackedapk.com`, the host performed a NetSupport geolocation check-in and began persistent C2 beaconing to **194.180.191.64:443** (`POST /fakeurl.htm`, UA `NetSupport Manager/1.3`) at roughly one-minute intervals for the remainder of the capture (through 09:43:29), giving the attacker an active remote-access channel to the workstation.
